title: svdg.org harvest returns a German recruitment agency page, not SVDG content
answer: This is the text harvested from svdg.org on 28 September 2026, and it is not Silicon Valley Defense Group material. It is a German language page for Motiv, an agency run by Andrej Schindler and Jonas von der Gathen that places creative people with values driven companies. The single useful point for a defense AI reader is negative: the harvest contains no mapping of commercial entrants, no defense content and no AI content, so the claim that SVDG maps companies driving AI adoption in the Department of Defense space cannot be checked against it.

sections.body: The text supplied is a German language landing page for Motiv, described as an agency for future potential, run by Andrej Schindler and Jonas von der Gathen. It is a commercial services page rather than a report, dataset or research document. It describes what the agency does, invites readers to register for a quarterly newsletter covering open positions, company visits and interviews, and sets out the agency's view of people and organisations. The harvest is dated 28 September 2026. The text itself states no publication date and carries no author byline beyond the two named principals. The page was harvested from the URL svdg.org, but nothing in the wording refers to Silicon Valley Defense Group, to defense, or to artificial intelligence.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page presents Motiv as an agency that connects creative people with values oriented companies and lists its services. It offers a quarterly newsletter with information on open positions, descriptions of company visits and interviews with people from different sectors. The agency says it connects people and companies, accompanies individual development and creates spaces for future perspectives, and describes perceiving what has already developed while sensing what is coming as both its capability and its daily challenge. Companies are understood as grown and unique organisms, where meaning and the drive to develop further are the motivating forces. Even when a company's purpose is deeply written into its history, the people and the forms of collaboration change. The stated aim is to place people who bring both the necessary technical competence and the ability to connect with a company's purpose. The agency treats people as developing beings and says its goal is to perceive individual potential and recognise the right moment for career steps. It works with companies holding social and ecological values and seeks long term working relationships, connecting and accompanying people looking for meaningful tasks and companies facing future challenges.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The text gives no numbers, no dates, no definitions of artificial intelligence or defense, and no data of any kind. The only named specifics are the two agency principals, Andrej Schindler and Jonas von der Gathen, and a quarterly newsletter covering open positions, company visits and interviews. Its only stated positions are that companies should be understood as grown and unique organisms, that it works with companies holding social and ecological values, and that it seeks long term working relationships.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in the defense industry would find nothing usable here. The page contains no companies, no capital flows, no Department of Defense programmes and no AI adoption data, so it cannot support the industry page claim that Silicon Valley Defense Group maps the commercial entrants driving AI adoption in the Department of Defense space. Its only value is as a warning: the harvested text does not match the cited URL, so that claim needs to be checked against a different and genuine source before it is relied on.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Defense

sections.body: This is a commercial agency landing page written in German, undated, and aimed at job seekers and client companies rather than at analysts. It covers no defense procurement, no AI policy, no investment and no market mapping. It is partial by design, since it exists to advertise services, and it offers no evidence, methodology or figures. Because the content does not correspond to the URL it was harvested from, it cannot verify anything about Silicon Valley Defense Group or its work.
